name: Μεγάλο Μαράθι
evidence: Messinia guides (Pylos, between Finikounda-Koroni) repeatedly call Mikro/Megalo Marathi 'two wonderful sandy beaches (αμμώδεις)'; disambiguated by Pylos/Tsapi dirt-road access matching lat/lng.

name: Μικρό Μαράθι
evidence: Same Messinia cove pair as Megalo Marathi: 'The beaches are sandy... two wonderful sandy beaches, small and large Marathi'; Pylos.info/pylos-area sources confirm.

name: Άγιος Παύλος
evidence: Amorgos guides: 'tongue of fine white pebbles' with 'a strip of sand extending into the sea', opposite Nikouria islet (matches lat/lng) - sand-and-pebble, not rock.

name: Καμπί
evidence: Amorgos (near Hozoviotissa/Agia Anna, matches lat/lng): 'coarse and fine pebbles', a small pebbled nudist cove - pebbles, not rock.

name: Foniadiko
evidence: Remote Ios beach ('Φοντάδικο', reached by dirt road branching toward Agia Theodoti) with no published composition data found; kept our label (ours and OSM both say sand).

name: Σαρακήνικο
evidence: Milos Sarakiniko (north coast, ~5km from Plaka, matches lat/lng): Wikipedia describes it as 'a narrow strip of sand between all-white volcanic rocks' - beach surface is sand though famed for surrounding white rock slabs.

name: Βούδια
evidence: Milos Voudia (near Pollonia, pink volcanic cliffs, matches lat/lng): 'pebbles beach... white pebble and pink sand', clear stones of various sizes mixed with light sand - mixed, leans pebbles, not pure sand.

name: Βίντζι
evidence: Naxos Chora, below Portara (matches lat/lng): the smaller Chora beach, 'small stretch of sand', a man-made sandy beach for a quick swim - sand, not rock (distinct from rocky Grotta next door).

name: Γρόττα
evidence: Naxos Chora north seaside (matches lat/lng): 'very rocky... a small bay strewn with a mixture of pebbles and some sand', for snorkeling rather than swimming - predominantly rock/pebble.

name: Δρυός
evidence: Paros SE coast settlement Dryos (matches lat/lng): 'the beach of Dryos consists of sand and pebbles' - mixed, not pure pebbles.

name: Αμπέλα
evidence: Syros SW near Megas Gialos (matches lat/lng): Greeka 'a small, sandy shore with some scattered pebbles... soft sand' - predominantly sand, not pebbles.

name: Παραλία Λωτό
evidence: Syros western coast Lotos (matches lat/lng): 'partly organized seashore with sand and pebbles... soft sand and pebbles around the shore' - mixed, not pure pebbles.

name: Κασόνια
evidence: Kalymnos town beach (Kasonia, closest to Pothia, matches lat/lng): 'a long sandy beach... strewn with sand and pebbles', with tamarisk trees - predominantly sand, not pebbles.

name: Ποτάλι
evidence: Karpathos west coast near Kato Lefkos (matches lat/lng): 'characterized by gray pebbles and coarse sand in some places', with some rocks at the sides in the sea - pebble/coarse-sand, not primarily rock.

name: Θερμά
evidence: Kos SE hot-springs beach (Embros Thermae after Agios Fokas, matches lat/lng): 'mostly covered with dark sand and stones... dark pebbles' from volcanic activity - mixed dark sand and pebbles/stones, not pure sand.

name: Κισσίρια
evidence: Obscure northern Lipsi beach (listed by name in the municipality/CityMobile catalog but with no composition description); no reliable surface source found, kept our label.

name: Κοίμηση
evidence: Lipsi, below the Church of Koimisis (SW/NW, reached via carved path, matches lat/lng): 'characterized by pebbles... pebble and gravel' - pebbles, not sand.

name: Κορακιά
evidence: Obscure eastern Lipsi cove not featured in any beach guide (Korakia hits return other regions - Lavreotiki/Crete); could not pin the Lipsi one, kept our label.

name: Πνιγμένος
evidence: Obscure Lipsi cove absent from all beach listings/guides; no composition source found, kept our label.

name: Στίφη
evidence: Obscure Lipsi cove absent from all beach listings/guides; no composition source found, kept our label.
